explanation: Energy enters ecosystems through photosynthesis. As organic nutrients are passed up the food chain from one level to the next, only a fraction of the energy is transferred. The vast majority of the energy is lost to the environment as heat, a pattern that strictly follows the Laws of Thermodynamics.

questions.q: What happens to the majority of energy as it is transferred from one level of the ecosystem to the next?
opts: It is completely destroyed and disappears from existence.
It is recycled back into the plants to increase photosynthesis rates.
It is lost to the environment as heat energy.
It is converted into chemical minerals within the soil.
questions.exp: The notes state that 'only a portion of the energy is transferred; The vast majority is lost as heat energy,' in accordance with the Laws of Thermodynamics.
